verses.text: Can you pull Leviathan out with a fishhook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
Can you run a rope through his nose or put a hook through his jaw?
Will he beg you over and over or speak softly to you?
Will he make a deal to serve you for the rest of his life?
Can you play with him like a pet bird or put him on a leash for your girls?
Will traders bargain over him and divide him among the merchants?
Can you cover his hide with barbed hooks or drive fishing spears into his head?
Just try laying a hand on him. You’ll remember the fight and never try again.
Any hope of catching him is useless. The sight of him alone is enough to bring you down.
No one is fierce enough to stir him up. So who can stand before me?
Who has ever given me anything that I owe them back? Everything under the sky is mine.
I won’t stay quiet about his limbs, his tremendous strength, or how well he’s built.
Who can strip off his outer armor? Who would dare come between his jaws?
Who can pry open the doors of his face? His teeth are terrifying from every side.
His rows of tough scales are his pride, sealed tightly together.
Each scale fits so close to the next that no air can pass between them.
They lock together so firmly that no one can pull them apart.
Light flashes when he sneezes, and his eyes gleam like the first light of dawn.
Burning torches shoot from his mouth, and sparks fly out.
Smoke pours from his nostrils like steam from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
His breath sets coals alight, and flames shoot from his mouth.
Strength fills his neck, and terror dances ahead of him.
The folds of his flesh fit together. They’re solid and won’t budge.
His heart is hard as stone, as hard as the lower millstone.
When he rises, even the mighty are afraid. They back away when he thrashes.
A sword can’t get through to him, and neither can a spear, a dart, or a pointed shaft.
Iron is like straw to him, and bronze is like rotten wood.
Arrows won’t drive him off. Sling stones are like husks blowing past him.
Clubs are just stubble to him, and he laughs when a javelin comes flying.
His belly is like sharp pieces of broken pottery, leaving tracks in the mud like a threshing sled.
He makes the deep churn like a boiling pot. He stirs the sea like ointment in a jar.
He leaves a shining trail behind him, as if the deep had turned white-haired.
There’s nothing on earth like him. He was made without fear.
He looks down on all that is lofty. He’s king over all who are proud.
